cause: Previously increased J4 PD gains induced or amplified a motor-local closed-loop oscillation at a fixed nominal target. Controlled gain changes strongly reduced it; the exact internal firmware/filter/compliance mechanism is unconfirmed.

J4_target_reconstruction.assumption: friction_scale=0, extra torque=0, positive kp with unclipped gravity offset; apply unchanged source gravity model and CAN quantization.
friction_scale=0, extra torque=0, positive kp with unclipped gravity offset; apply unchanged source gravity model and CAN quantization.

whole_trial_target_reconstruction.assumption: All ordinary joint readings remain constant; same gravity/zero-friction assumptions as phase reconstruction.

method.audio_PSD: Welch Hann 2 s windows, 50% overlap, 0.5 Hz bins; channel 1; PSD-integrated band power in dBFS. No weighting/normalization to peaks.
method.CAN_PSD: Native timestamp-selected samples, measured average rate around100Hz, Welch2s, DC removed.
method.latency: Audio clock origin uses process start timestamp. Device latency is uncalibrated; no exact cross-sensor phase claim. Extra inner-window +/-0.25 s origin sensitivity is reported.
method.limits: Ambient uncalibrated microphone: not dB SPL. Baseline3s vs candidate7s; no noise-source isolation, no inference that all environmental noise belongs to J4. Harmonic labels are frequency neighborhoods, not proof of common origin.

measurement_limits: 100 Hz motor feedback cannot uniquely resolve mechanical frequencies above 50 Hz.
Zero speed feedback means zero at that feedback resolution, not proof of zero mechanical vibration.
Camera 90 fps did not reliably resolve subpixel mechanical vibration beyond background registration noise.
Microphone levels and start latency are uncalibrated; ambient broadband sound is not uniquely sourced to the robot.
Ordinary joint angles and motor position use different resolutions/offsets; lowering kp can change motor position despite unchanged ordinary position packets.
Trials cover this arm, tool and small low-speed paths; target speed cap is not a hard physical velocity limit.
simulation_fix: Evaluate physical friction at each 1 ms physics substep instead of holding it for the 5 ms control interval. Host compensation stays 200 Hz. This corrects a separate numerical artifact, not the physical-arm root cause.
